description: DFA five-tuple encoded as Python dict with states, start, accept, delta (dict of dicts). run_dfa is a generic 10-line runner that takes any machine dict. Two machines: EVEN_ONES (2 states) and THREE_AS_DFA (4 states). Dead state handled by early return on missing transition.

steps.description: EVEN_ONES machine dict: states={'even','odd'}, start='even', accept={'even'}, delta maps state->char->next_state. 'even': 0->even, 1->odd. 'odd': 0->odd, 1->even.

run_dfa generic runner: gets start state, loops over input chars. Checks if ch in delta[state]; if not, returns False (dead state). Otherwise updates state = delta[state][ch]. After loop, returns True if state in accept set.
Dead state guard: machine['delta'].get(state, {}) returns empty dict for missing state, so ch not in {} triggers early return False without naming an explicit trap state.

steps.answer: start state 'even' is in accept set, and the loop body never runs for empty input
steps.question: Why does EVEN_ONES accept the empty string?

steps.description: Test loop runs EVEN_ONES on 7 strings. Then trace run on '1011' shows step-by-step transitions.
THREE_AS_DFA machine: start='q0', accept={'q3'}. delta: q0 a->q1, b->q0; q1 a->q2, b->q0; q2 a->q3, b->q0; q3 a->q3, b->q3 (absorbing accept). q2 on b goes to q0 because run of a's broken.
q3 loops to itself on both inputs: once three a's seen, machine never leaves accept state.
Trace '1011': start even, '1'->odd, '0'->odd, '1'->even, '1'->odd, final odd REJECT.

title: DFA as Dictionary Data: Generic Runner with Machine Data
